shlokas.sanskrit: तयोः संवदतोरेवं रामलक्ष्मणयोस्तदा । वासन्तिकी निशा प्राप्ता न शीता न च घर्मदा ।। 7.60.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tayoḥ saṃvadatorevaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇayostadā | vāsantikī niśā prāptā na śītā na ca gharmadā || 7.60.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: While Rama and Lakshmana were conversing together in this way, the night of springtime came on, neither cold nor bringing heat.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतपौर्वाह्णिकक्रियः । अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थो दर्शनं पौरकार्यवित् ।। 7.60.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ prabhāte vimale kṛtapaurvāhṇikakriyaḥ | abhicakrāma kākutstho darśanaṃ paurakāryavit || 7.60.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then, when the spotless dawn had broken and he had performed his morning rites, Kakutstha (Rama), knowing the affairs of the citizens, went forth to give audience.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः सुमन्त्रस्त्वागम्य राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । एते प्रतिहता राजन्द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति तापसाः ।। 7.60.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ sumantrastvāgamya rāghavaṃ vākyamabravīt | ete pratihatā rājandvāri tiṣṭhanti tāpasāḥ || 7.60.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Sumantra, having approached Raghava, spoke these words: "O king, these ascetics, having been detained, are waiting at the gate."

shlokas.sanskrit: भार्गवच्यवनं चैव पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः । दर्शनं ते महाराज्ञश्चोदयन्ति कृतत्वराः । प्रीयमाणा नरव्याघ्र यमुनातीरवासिनः ।। 7.60.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bhārgavacyavanaṃ caiva puraskṛtya maharṣayaḥ | darśanaṃ te mahārājñaścodayanti kṛtatvarāḥ | prīyamāṇā naravyāghra yamunātīravāsinaḥ || 7.60.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Placing Chyavana of the Bhrigu line at their head, the great sages, in eager haste, urge that you, the great king, grant them audience; O tiger among men, they who dwell on the bank of the Yamuna are well disposed toward you."

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामः प्रोवाच धर्मवित् । प्रवेश्यन्तां महाभागा भार्गवप्रमुखा द्विजाः ।। 7.60.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāmaḥ provāca dharmavit | praveśyantāṃ mahābhāgā bhārgavapramukhā dvijāḥ || 7.60.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard his words, Rama, knower of dharma, replied: "Let the illustrious twice-born ones, with Bhargava (Chyavana) foremost among them, be ushered in."

shlokas.sanskrit: राज्ञस्त्वाज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । प्रवेशयामास तदा तापसान्सुदुरासदान् ।। 7.60.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rājñastvājñāṃ puraskṛtya dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ | praveśayāmāsa tadā tāpasānsudurāsadān || 7.60.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the gatekeeper, placing the king's command above all, with his palms joined upon his head, ushered in the ascetics, who were exceedingly hard to approach.

shlokas.sanskrit: शतं समधिकं तत्र दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । प्रविष्टं राजभवनं तापसानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.60.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śataṃ samadhikaṃ tatra dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā | praviṣṭaṃ rājabhavanaṃ tāpasānāṃ mahātmanām || 7.60.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: There more than a hundred of those great-souled ascetics, blazing with their own radiance, entered the royal palace.

shlokas.sanskrit: ते द्विजाः पूर्णकलशैः सर्वतीर्थाम्बुसत्कृतैः । गृहीत्वा फलमूलं च रामस्याभ्याहरन्बहु ।। 7.60.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te dvijāḥ pūrṇakalaśaiḥ sarvatīrthāmbusatkṛtaiḥ | gṛhītvā phalamūlaṃ ca rāmasyābhyāharanbahu || 7.60.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Those twice-born ones, taking full pitchers honored with the waters of all the sacred fords, and fruits and roots, brought much of these as offerings to Rama.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य तु तत्सर्वं रामः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः । तीर्थोदकानि सर्वाणि फलानि विविधानि च ।। 7.60.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pratigṛhya tu tatsarvaṃ rāmaḥ prītipuraskṛtaḥ | tīrthodakāni sarvāṇi phalāni vividhāni ca || 7.60.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And Rama, filled with affection, received all of that—all the waters of the sacred fords and the fruits of various kinds.

shlokas.sanskrit: उवाच च महाबाहुः सर्वानेव महामुनीन् । इमान्यासनमुख्यानि यथार्हमुपविश्यताम् ।। 7.60.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: uvāca ca mahābāhuḥ sarvāneva mahāmunīn | imānyāsanamukhyāni yathārhamupaviśyatām || 7.60.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the mighty-armed one spoke to all those great sages: "Let each be seated upon these excellent seats according to his rank."

shlokas.sanskrit: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महर्षयः । बृसीषु रुचिराख्यासु निषेदुः काञ्चनीषु ते ।। 7.60.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā sarva eva maharṣayaḥ | bṛsīṣu rucirākhyāsu niṣeduḥ kāñcanīṣu te || 7.60.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard Rama's words, all those great sages seated themselves upon those golden cushions called beautiful seats.

shlokas.sanskrit: उपविष्टानृषींस्तत्र दृष्ट्वा परपुरञ्जयः । प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.60.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: upaviṣṭānṛṣīṃstatra dṛṣṭvā parapurañjayaḥ | prayataḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā rāghavo vākyamabravīt || 7.60.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Seeing the sages seated there, Raghava, conqueror of hostile cities, becoming reverent and with palms joined, spoke these words:

shlokas.sanskrit: किमागमनकार्यं वः किं करोमि समाहितः । आज्ञाप्यो ऽहं महर्षीणां सर्वकामकरः सुखम् ।। 7.60.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kimāgamanakāryaṃ vaḥ kiṃ karomi samāhitaḥ | ājñāpyo 'haṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sarvakāmakaraḥ sukham || 7.60.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "What is the purpose of your coming? What may I do, attentive as I am? Let me be commanded by the great sages; I am gladly the fulfiller of every wish."

shlokas.sanskrit: इदं राज्यं च सकलं जीवितं च हृदि स्थितम् । सर्वमेतद्द्विदार्थं मे सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि वः ।। 7.60.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: idaṃ rājyaṃ ca sakalaṃ jīvitaṃ ca hṛdi sthitam | sarvametaddvidārthaṃ me satyametadbravīmi vaḥ || 7.60.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This entire kingdom, and my very life that abides in my heart—all of this is for the sake of the twice-born; this truth I declare to you."

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा साधुकारो महानभूत् । ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां यमुनातीरवासिनाम् ।। 7.60.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sādhukāro mahānabhūt | ṛṣīṇāmugratapasāṃ yamunātīravāsinām || 7.60.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing those words of his, a great cry of approval arose from the sages of fierce austerities who dwelt on the bank of the Yamuna.

shlokas.sanskrit: ऊचुश्च ते महात्मानो हर्षेण महता वृताः । उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ तवैव भुवि नान्यतः ।। 7.60.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ūcuśca te mahātmāno harṣeṇa mahatā vṛtāḥ | upapannaṃ naraśreṣṭha tavaiva bhuvi nānyataḥ || 7.60.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And those great-souled ones, filled with great joy, said: "This is fitting for you alone upon the earth, O best of men, and for none other."

shlokas.sanskrit: बहवः पार्थिवा राजन्नतिक्रान्ता महाबलाः । कार्यस्य गौरवं मत्वा प्रतिज्ञां नाभ्यरोचयन् ।। 7.60.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bahavaḥ pārthivā rājannatikrāntā mahābalāḥ | kāryasya gauravaṃ matvā pratijñāṃ nābhyarocayan || 7.60.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Many mighty kings before you, O king, have passed away, for, weighing the gravity of the task, they did not consent to such a vow."

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वया पुनर्ब्राह्मणगौरवादियं कृता प्रतिज्ञा ह्यनवेक्ष्य कारणम् । ततश्च कर्ता ह्यसि नात्र संशयो महाभयात्ऺत्रातुमृषींस्त्वमर्हसि ।। 7.60.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tvayā punarbrāhmaṇagauravādiyaṃ kṛtā pratijñā hyanavekṣya kāraṇam | tataśca kartā hyasi nātra saṃśayo mahābhayātऺtrātumṛṣīṃstvamarhasi || 7.60.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "But you, out of reverence for the brahmins, have made this vow without considering the cause; therefore you will surely accomplish it, of this there is no doubt. You are worthy to deliver the sages from this great peril."

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 60 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe ṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ || 60 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the sixtieth canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the glorious Ramayana, the first poem composed by the seer Valmiki.
